title: Swap a drone's chipped propeller: hold the prop still while unscrewing its nut, then fit and tighten the new one
instruction: Replace the drone's chipped propeller with the new one on the stand. Hold the chipped propeller still by a blade with one hand while the other hand unscrews its red nut (anticlockwise) and lifts it off; put the chipped propeller in the blue bin; set the new propeller on the same motor, printed side up, then hold it still by a blade while you screw the nut back on (clockwise) until it is tight. Then take both arms back to where they started.
context: Inspection, mapping and delivery drones fly fleets of robots that need their propellers swapped after every nick, since a chipped blade shakes the airframe and can shed pieces. The motor spins freely when it is off, so a technician holds the propeller still with one hand while the other turns the nut: a routine two-handed job that today needs a person at every landing pad.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A quadcopter drone, fixed in place on its skids: a dark grey ABS body 17 by 11 cm with a battery strapped on top and a camera gimbal under its front, centred 54 cm forward and 2 cm right, and four black carbon-fibre arms in a '+' to four brushless motors 24 cm from the centre, each with an orange propeller and a red prop nut. The rear motor, nearest the arms, is the one to service: its axis 30 cm forward and 2 cm right; its aluminium bell, 3.2 cm across, turns freely (the motor is off), its top 8.7 cm above the table, with a 16 mm steel centring spigot and a 10 mm steel threaded shaft standing 16 mm above the propeller's hub. (2) On it, the chipped propeller: orange glass-filled nylon, 30 cm tip to tip, its blades running left-right, its hub 3.6 cm square and 1.6 cm tall with a 2.4 cm hole; the tip of its right blade is broken off (2.2 cm short) with a crack. (3) Clamping it, a red anodised aluminium bullet nut: a 19 mm hex, 3.8 cm tall with its washer flange (2.9 cm across) and dome, screwed down tight. (4) A new propeller of the same kind, its blades' tops printed with white size marks, lying printed side up with its blades left-right on a grey steel stand (a post with a square peg in its hub) centred 27 cm forward and 30 cm right, its hub's bottom 7.4 cm above the table. (5) A blue polypropylene bin for worn parts, inside 12 by 36 cm (long side left-right) with 3.5 cm walls, centred 16 cm forward on the centre line. (6) A stainless steel parts dish, inside 6 cm square with 1.2 cm walls, centred 20 cm forward and 24 cm right. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end, except "came off", which counts at any time. Came off: the nut was unscrewed off the end of the motor's thread at some point. 1.0: the nut came off, the chipped propeller lies in the blue bin, the new propeller sits on the motor's spigot (its hub within 8 mm of the motor's axis and 4 mm of the bell's top, printed side up within 8 degrees), the nut is screwed down on it and tight (seated within 0.8 mm and turned on until the thread pulls it at least 0.6 mm into its seat), and both arms are back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.5: the nut came off, the chipped propeller is in the bin, the new propeller sits on the spigot and the nut has caught the thread; 0.25: the nut came off at some point; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the new propeller and the nut still.
reset_notes: Take the nut off, put the new propeller back on its stand and the chipped one back on the motor, and screw the nut down tight on it.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the thread is a joint keeping the nut on the shaft plus a spring the task file moves 13.5 mm per turn of the nut against the bell; the nut comes off 8 mm up and catches again when set back on the shaft. The motor is a hinge with light drag; only friction under the hub and the nut couples the propeller to it. The airframe is one fixed body. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
